Arjun Mehta: flagging an incident from a private on‑prem install (tenant: HarborHealth). After a scheduled KMS rotation two services returned 403 decrypts for ~8 minutes. Seeing this across two separate clusters.
Leah Kim: did the rotation include any network policy changes or was it KMS-only?
Arjun Mehta: KMS-only. Rotation job run at 2026-02-20T08:12 UTC. Errors start 08:13.
sec-bot: Alert: decrypt_403 spike for tenant=harborhealth at 2026-02-20T08:13:05Z. Audit id: rot-20260220-0812.
Infra Ops: paste keystore-proxy logs (sanitized):
```
2026-02-20T08:13:06Z keystore-proxy ERROR tenant=harborhealth msg="decrypt denied" code=403 key=kms://harbor/key-v3 principal=svc-harbor-proxy
2026-02-20T08:13:07Z hsm-connector WARN principal-check failed: principal not present in key policy
```
Tara Chen: hmm similar pattern to other rotate races, but the odd bit: we saw partial principal propagation to one cluster and not the other even though automation hit both. Could be a transactional ordering issue.
Leah Kim: which infra-agent version? any CRD backpressure?
sec-bot: Rotation metadata: infra-agent v2.2.0 executed rotation. Two clusters: cluster-a and cluster-b. Propagation logs show cluster-a policy patched at 08:12:50, cluster-b patched at 08:20:05. Alias flip occurred at 08:12:45 globally.
Arjun Mehta: so alias flipped before cluster-b had principals. That explains the 403s on cluster-b until manual grant. Why did alias flip globally before per-cluster policies applied?
Infra Ops: rotation job is multi-target: create new key versions, update alias globally, then iterate clusters to patch per-cluster principal lists. We need to flip ordering to ensure per-cluster principal parity before alias swap.
Tara Chen: agreed. Mitigation executed: manual grant to cluster-b keys and we validated app decrypts at 08:21. Command used: `kmsctl grant --key key-v3 --principal svc-harbor-proxy --actions decrypt` -> exit 0.
Leah Kim: action items: 1) change rotation workflow to propagate principals to all affected clusters first, then atomically flip aliases (or use a staged alias switch per-cluster), 2) add a pre-swap check asserting every cluster reports principal_present=true, fail-safe to rollback alias if parity not reached, 3) add automated test in infra-agent e2e to simulate high api latency and verify ordering, 4) add tenant alert: >5 decrypt 403s in 5m triggers immediate pause of rotation jobs.
sec-bot: security note: limit service principal scope to tenant-only key ARNs and require mTLS auth for keystore-proxy. Also add audit entry recording per-cluster propagation times for compliance.
Infra Ops: I'll draft a hotfix to reorder steps and a migration guide for on-prem customers (some may rely on global alias semantics). Patch target: hotfix in 48h, full rollout across infra-agent fleet in 2 weeks.
Tara Chen: for incident write-up include: timeline, affected clusters, manual remediation commands, audit artifacts, customer communication draft.
Arjun Mehta: customer comms draft: "We've identified a sequencing issue in our key rotation workflow for multi-cluster private installs that briefly removed decrypt permissions on some clusters. We applied a manual fix; a hotfix will be released within 48 hours and a full rollout in 2 weeks. No secret material was exposed. Audit trail attached."
Leah Kim: small security enhancement: keystore-proxy should treat 403s during rotation as a special-case transient error and retry with exponential backoff for 2 minutes before surfacing a hard failure to calling apps. This reduces apparent outage during brief propagation lag.
Infra Ops: noted. Creating GH issues INF-4701 (rotation-order-hotfix), INF-4702 (preflight-parity-check), INF-4703 (403-rate-alert), INF-4704 (keystore-proxy-transient-retry).
sec-bot: Attachments: rotation job logs, per-cluster propagation timestamps, netflow captures (no netpol denies).
Arjun Mehta: thanks team. I'll link the postmortem in #eng-security and notify the customer success lead. :thumbsup:
